Subject: Dedicated capacity — compute trajectory & prompt-mix audit request

Hi Lina / Jordan,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — great product. To get a concrete Dedicated sizing proposal over the next 6–12 months we need a bit more granularity on the traffic and prompt mix. Can you complete/confirm the quick items below and attach any existing traffic reports you have? The more specific the distributions the better our SKU + warm-pool recommendation will be.

Key asks:
- Peak concurrency (requests/sec) and typical burst shape (duration of burst, % uplift vs baseline).
- Expected ramp profile: approximate % of final traffic by week for the first 12 weeks (or month-by-month).
- Prompt/response token distribution: for each flow type (chat, Q&A, summarize, embed), provide mean and 90th pct for prompt and generated tokens.
- Session behavior: average session duration, % of multi-turn sessions, KV/cache re-use rate, and whether you use persistent conversation IDs.
- Latency SLO targets: p50/p95/p99 generation latency (at cold and warm conditions). Tail targets are particularly important.
- Acceptable cost envelope or price sensitivity for reserved capacity (helps us recommend A100/H100 vs mixed fleet).
- Any security / regional residency constraints for the private deployment.

Attachments you can include: sampled request logs, token histograms, representative prompts, and any forecast spreadsheets. We typically convert those into a compute-trajectory model (tokens/sec and KV cache hit assumptions) and return a short SKU + reserved capacity map with an expected monthly cost delta vs hosted.

If easier, drop a CSV with columns: flow_type, timestamp, requests, prompt_tokens_mean, response_tokens_mean, cache_reuse_pct, and we’ll run that through the sizing engine.

I’ve attached our short intake worksheet to make it easier. I’ll loop in Marissa (performance sizing) and Karthik (cluster plan) for the follow-up.

Best,

Sean Gallagher
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Hey Sean — thanks, this is exactly the kind of checklist we were hoping for. Attaching two items: sample_prompts.txt (500 lines sampled across flows) and acme_compute_profile.csv (last 30 days aggregated by minute). Quick answers below; we can sync if you want live walk-through.

Short profile summary (high level):
- Baseline: 450 reqs/s; Peak sustained: 2,000 reqs/s; Peak burst observed: 5,100 reqs/s for short windows (~12–20 minutes) during marketing pushes.
- Ramp plan (go-live to 90 days): week1 ~8%, week2 ~20%, week3 ~40%, week4 ~60%, week8 ~85%, week12 ~100% (we expect staged rollouts by region).
- Flow breakdown by volume: chat 62%, Q&A 18%, summarization/batch 12%, embeddings 8%.
- Token stats (mean / 90th):
  - Chat prompts: 110 / 290 tokens; chat responses: 560 / 1,900 tokens (long tails when code or long context returned).
  - Q&A prompts: 60 / 120; responses: 180 / 600.
  - Summarize prompts (batch jobs): 3,500 / 7,200 prompt tokens; responses: 200 / 400 (we stream).
  - Embeddings: 450 tokens per item, batched.
- Session behavior: 48% multi-turn sessions, median session length 7 messages, cache reuse estimated ~38% for short-term context and ~15% persistent reuse across sessions.
- Target SLOs: p50 120ms token, p95 550ms token, p99 1.2s token for warm traffic. Cold starts acceptable up to 2.5s token for rare requests.
- Cost sensitivity: priority is meeting latency SLOs; willing to trade ~20% higher OPEX for predictable p99.
- Data residency: US-only for initial rollouts; some EU customers later. SOC2 in place; happy to share questionnaire.

We’ve included the CSV — note that minutes with campaign pushes show a heavy left-skew (many small requests with intermittent huge summarize jobs). Let me know if you want a zoom to walk through the CSV.

Thanks,
Lina Park

Looping you both in with a quick first-pass sizing note based on Lina’s numbers.

(Forwarded message below)

Quick sizing hypothesis (very conservative):
- Traffic model: base 450 req/s, steady peak 2k req/s, short burst to 5k req/s for ~15 minutes. Include a 1.25x safety buffer on bursts for reserved capacity planning.
- Token load: weighted mean tokens/sec at peak ~ (chat 62% * (110+560) + rest) ≈ 1.2M tokens/sec (approx).
- Cache benefits: assuming 38% short-term reuse we estimate effective token reduction ~22–28% depending on prefix alignment; for chat-heavy workloads this materially reduces per-token GPU time.
- Recommended starter fleet (US):
  - Option A (latency-first): 12 x H100 (full-reserved) + 4 x A10G warm pool for burst absorption.
  - Option B (cost-balanced): 18 x A100/A10G mix with autoscale to H100 transiently for extreme tails.
- Warm pool / pre-warm: maintain ~15% warm pool to keep KV warm for high-cache-reuse flows (reduces cold-p99 events).
- Batching strategy: prioritize continuous batching on A100-class nodes for embeddings & summarize jobs; isolate chat on H100-like nodes for best p99.

Open questions we need ACME to confirm before we finalize a proposal:
1) Exact fraction of summarize batch jobs that can be scheduled off-peak vs must be synchronous.
2) Whether persistent conversation IDs are required for >30 days (affects cache footprint).
3) Acceptance threshold for p99 during burst windows (is 1.2s hard limit or negotiable).

If we get those answers I’ll run through cost curves and a 12-week ramp plan (including commit levels and reserved vs burstable mix). Also suggest a 60-minute sizing workshop with their infra/ops folks — I can lead the technical portion and Karthik can map to topology and autoscale rules.

—Marissa
